As an AI Engineer at Nelnet, you'll be at the intersection of applied AI and software engineering. Your primary focus will be twofold: keeping our existing fleet of deployed agents healthy, evaluated, and improving over time, and designing new agentic capabilities that extend what those systems can do. Beyond building, you'll help expand the agentic approach across the organization, partnering with business stakeholders to identify high-value use cases, establishing reusable patterns and guardrails, and raising the bar for how teams evaluate and ship AI systems. Agent Development: Design, build, and deploy LLM-powered agents to solve concrete business problems. This includes tool use, multi-step reasoning, orchestration, and human-in-the-loop patterns.

Evaluation: Build and maintain evaluation suites for agent systems, including offline test sets, LLM-as-judge scoring, regression testing, and online metrics.
Observability and Monitoring: Instrument agents end to end, including traces, tool calls, token usage, latency, cost, and outcome quality and act on what the data shows.
Context and Retrieval Engineering: Design retrieval and context strategies (RAG, structured data access, caching, chunking, ranking) that give agents the right information at the right time.
Tooling and Integrations: Build and maintain the tools, APIs, and connectors agents rely on, ensuring safe and reliable interaction with internal systems and data.
Scalability and Infrastructure: Design and implement scalable AI pipelines and services on AWS, using infrastructure as code (Terraform) and CI/CD to automate deployment and maintenance.
Guardrails and Responsible AI: Implement safety controls, input/output validation, access boundaries, and audit trails appropriate to a regulated environment.
Expanding Agentic Adoption: Partner with teams across the organization to identify where agents add real value, prototype quickly, and turn one-off wins into reusable frameworks and standards.
Documentation: Maintain clear documentation of agent architectures, prompts, tool contracts, data flows, evaluation results, and known limitations.
Innovation: Track the fast-moving foundation model and agent tooling landscape, and bring what's genuinely useful into our stack.
Mentorship: Provide guidance to team members on agent design, evaluation practices, and applied AI best practices.

Strong programming skills in Python.
Working knowledge of AWS services for AI workloads (e.g., Bedrock, Lambda, ECS/Fargate, S3, OpenSearch, Step Functions).
Familiarity with agent frameworks and orchestration tooling, and sound judgment about when a framework helps versus when to build directly.
Practical prompt and context engineering skill, with an evaluation-driven approach to improving them.
Experience with infrastructure as code (IaC) tools like Terraform.
Proficiency using CI/CD pipelines to automate testing and deployment of AI workflows.
Experience with containerization technologies like Docker and orchestration tools like Kubernetes.
Solid grounding in machine learning fundamentals and statistical reasoning, sufficient to evaluate systems rigorously and know when a non-LLM approach is the better answer.
Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work in a collaborative environment.
Strong critical thinking, analytical, and quantitative problem-solving ability.

description_preview:
LabACT helps biotech and pharmaceutical teams turn complex scientific and operational problems into working software.
We work directly with scientists, informatics teams, data teams, and business leaders to understand how work actually gets done, identify where technology can make a meaningful difference, and build practical systems that fit into real scientific environments.
We are looking for a Forward Deployed Scientific Software Engineer who can operate at that intersection.
The Role
This is a hands-on software engineering role for someone who likes solving messy, important problems.
You will work directly with biotech and pharmaceutical teams to understand scientific workflows, data, systems, and constraints. You will then design and build software that improves those workflows.
Some problems will start with a clear specification. Many will not.
You may begin with a scientist describing a repetitive process, an Excel workbook that has become critical infrastructure, a collection of disconnected data sources, a legacy scientific application, or an idea for using AI that nobody has turned into a reliable system yet.
Your job is to figure out what to build and then help build it.
You will stay close to the people using the software, iterate quickly, and take solutions from initial discovery through production deployment.
This is a consulting role where the primary output is working software.
Job Function
Embed with biotech and pharmaceutical teams to understand scientific, technical, and operational workflows.
Translate ambiguous problems into clear technical requirements and practical implementation plans.
Design, prototype, build, test, and deploy production software.
Build scientific web applications, APIs, data pipelines, workflow automation, integrations, and internal tools.
Connect systems across scientific data sources, databases, cloud infrastructure, vendor platforms, and existing enterprise applications.
Apply AI and machine learning where they provide a real advantage, while recognizing when conventional software is the better solution.
Work directly with scientists, computational researchers, informatics teams, software engineers, and business stakeholders.
Investigate unfamiliar scientific domains and become productive quickly.
Modernize or replace fragile spreadsheets, scripts, manual processes, and legacy applications.
Design systems with appropriate attention to data provenance, reproducibility, security, auditability, and validation.
Troubleshoot problems across application code, data, infrastructure, networking, and deployment environments.
Document systems well enough that client teams can understand, operate, and extend them.
Identify patterns across engagements that can become reusable LabACT tools, architectures, and engineering practices.
What We're Looking For
We care more about what you can build and how you approach problems than whether your background follows a specific path.
Strong candidates will have:
Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience shipping production systems.
Proficiency in Python and experience with modern application development.
Experience with some combination of TypeScript/JavaScript, React, Node.js, SQL, REST APIs, and modern software frameworks.
Experience working with relational databases and complex data.
Practical cloud experience, particularly AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Experience with containers, CI/CD, source control, automated testing, and production deployment.
The ability to move comfortably between frontend, backend, data, infrastructure, and integration work as needed.
Strong debugging skills and the persistence to work through unfamiliar systems.
The ability to communicate clearly with both highly technical and non-technical people.
Comfort working directly with clients and asking enough questions to understand the problem behind the request.
Good technical judgment. You know when to build something sophisticated and when a simple solution is better.
Scientific Experience
Experience in biotech, pharmaceutical R&D, scientific informatics, computational biology, chemistry, clinical development, translational research, or another scientific software environment is highly valuable.
You should be comfortable sitting with a scientist, learning how their work is done, understanding enough of the science and data to ask good questions, and translating that knowledge into software.
AI
AI is increasingly part of the systems we build, but this is far from an AI-only engineering role.
You may work with LLMs, agents, retrieval systems, scientific models, evaluation frameworks, and AI-assisted workflows. You may also solve a problem with Python, PostgreSQL, React, AWS, and a well-designed API.
We care about choosing the right technology for each solution.
What Makes This Role Different
A traditional software engineer is often given a defined problem and builds against a product roadmap.
A consultant may analyze a problem and recommend what to do.
A Forward Deployed Scientific Software Engineer does both discovery and execution.
You might spend the morning working with scientists to understand why an existing workflow takes four hours, the afternoon tracing data through three systems, and the next several days building and deploying the application that reduces that workflow to minutes.
You are expected to understand the problem, make technical decisions, write the code, and help get the solution into people's hands.
You May Be a Great Fit If
You enjoy walking into situations where the answer is not obvious.
You like talking to users as much as you like building solutions.
You can work independently without disappearing into a technical silo.
You are comfortable saying, "I do not understand that yet," and then learning.
You care about shipping useful systems that people use to improve their work.

Location: Anywhere in Country
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.
We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.
At EY, our purpose is to shape the future. The insights and quality services we provide help build trust and confidence in the capital markets and economies all over the world. We develop outstanding leaders who are teamed to deliver our promises to all our stakeholders. In so doing, we play a critical role in building a better working world for our people, for our clients and for our communities.
The opportunity
The Platforms Practice specializes in mission-critical, intelligent platforms for the world’s most ambitious organizations. Using our product-driven, AI-centric approach, we empower organizations to build for the intelligent digital future. Our elite team of product leaders, data scientists, designers, and software engineers enable our clients to solve their most complex product challenges and positively impact people and the world. Software engineers are problem solvers. While most have deep expertise in specific areas of the technology stack (front end, back end, data, security etc.), all are comfortable swimming across lanes. This is really important in delivering the product and platform outcomes that our customers expect.
In this role, you will identify and define user/customer requirements, focusing on developing user interfaces (UI) across various platforms such as mobile, web, and tablets. You will be responsible for creating software components and services that interact seamlessly with upstream and downstream components, ensuring that business requirements are met through effective coding and programming.
Your Key Responsibilities
As a Senior Application Designer and Developer, you will play a pivotal role in delivering innovative solutions. Your time will be spent on various responsibilities, including:
Collaborating with clients to gather and analyze requirements, ensuring that the final product meets their needs.
Designing and developing user interfaces that are not only functional but also enhance user experience.
Writing clean, maintainable code and creating specifications that support business objectives.
Regular travel may be required to meet with clients, providing you with the opportunity to engage directly with stakeholders.
Skills And Attributes For Success
To excel in this role, you should possess a blend of technical and interpersonal skills. The following attributes will make a significant impact:
Translate business requirements into technical design and architecture
Develop prototypes and demos quickly
Function as part of an agile delivery process
Work on distributed systems problems ranging from scheduling, resource management, messaging, distributed caching and infrastructure automation
Solve sophisticated data and analytics problems at scale
Apply machine learning and AI systems to real-world business problems
Build world-class user experiences across a range of interfaces
Create automation systems for testing, continuous integration and continuous deployment
Design APIs and extensibility models for platform use cases that haven’t yet been imagined
Teach our clients how to build and deliver commercial software and services at scale
Strong understanding of agile delivery and development methodologies.
Proficiency in application development tools and quality assurance practices.
Ability to build and manage relationships with clients, fostering trust and value.
Excellent communication skills, capable of conveying complex ideas with clarity.
To qualify for the role, you must have
A Bachelor’s degree required (4-year degree).
Typically, no less than 2 - 4 years relevant experience.
3-5+ years of experience with Angular or similar frontend frameworks
Strong knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript, Angular
Knowledge of PostgreSQL and Temporal
Knowledge of Generative AI and building Agents
Ability to design and implement robust APIs and microservices using Java, Python, FastAPI and OpenAPI
Integrate authentication and authorization mechanisms using Keycloak, OAuth2, OIDC, and Azure Active Directory (AAD)
Experience with Data Visualization tools like: D3, Highcharts, Ploty.js, Ember Charts
Experience using Commercial Dashboards (PowerBI, Tableau, Looker)
Experience with Test-Driven Development (TDD) / unit testing
Experience working on complex problems and in a complex codebase
Knowledge of frontend “best practices” around page performance
Ideally, you’ll also have
A passion for delivering commercial software products and platforms to market
Be deeply technical and constantly in a state of learning
Able to communicate clearly and efficiently with a variety of audiences including developers, clients, customers, partners and executives
Fearless in getting “hands-on” with technology and execution
Strong understanding of modern software engineering processes
Deep understanding and interest in cloud and distributed systems architectures
Comfortable with ambiguity with a drive for clarity
Experience leading and growing technical talent (for software engineering managers)
Experience in complex problem-solving and critical thinking.
Strong emotional agility and the ability to collaborate in hybrid environments.
A proactive approach to learning and adapting to new technologies.
What We Look For
We seek individuals who are not only technically proficient but also possess a strong sense of curiosity and a desire to learn. Top performers are those who can navigate complex challenges with ease, communicate effectively, and build meaningful relationships with clients and colleagues alike.
What We Offer You
At EY, we’ll develop you with future-focused skills and equip you with world-class experiences. We’ll empower you in a flexible environment, and fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive cultur
